technical_issues.issue: The estimates 2,698 km / 560 km ≈ 5 and 2,698 km / 60 km ≈ 45 are dimensionless ratios, not days. They use adjacent-track spacing without establishing how the ground-track pattern shifts or repeats over time. The stated five-day access and 45-day mosaic are therefore unsupported; the STK figures show ground tracks, not sensor access or coverage of the reef.

A 50 Mbit/s downlink capacity is assumed without a link budget. Antenna gains, transmit power, frequency allocation, modulation/coding, losses and link margin are not established, so the claimed daily capacity margin is unverified.

The 0.10 m aperture is compared only with an ideal diffraction limit at 0.5 µm. That calculation alone does not establish 5 m multispectral image resolution or GSD; focal length, detector sampling, optical performance and signal-to-noise are not demonstrated.

The drag-sail lifetime estimate uses a simplified constant-density, scale-height model. The report acknowledges large solar-cycle variation, but does not provide a bounded lifetime analysis that verifies disposal within 25 years across environmental uncertainty.

overall: A strong, well-structured mission report with a clear Australian benefit, substantial design work and useful STK evidence. The principal weakness is the unsupported, dimensionally incorrect revisit and mosaic timing; the payload-performance and downlink assumptions also need verification.
